title: The proper case: direct images of proper morphisms
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a positive integer $N$. Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], where $S$ is of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $N$ is invertible on $S$, as in [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]. For every geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], write $X_{\bar s}=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose all these geometric fibres have dimension at most $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $F$ be a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Then $R^qf_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is constructible on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ for every $q\geq0$, and $R^qf_*F=0$ for $q>2d$.

proof.text: Properness includes finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Choose a finite affine cover $S=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with each $A_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. By the finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], each $f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A_i)$ has a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_{ij}$ with $B_{ij}$ finitely generated over $A_i$. The union of these covers is finite. Generators of $A_i$ over $k$ together with generators of $B_{ij}$ over $A_i$ generate $B_{ij}$ over $k$. Thus $X$ is of finite type over $k$; no separatedness of $S$ over $k$ is being assumed.

The image of a unit under a ring map is a unit, so invertibility of $N$ on $S$ implies invertibility on $X$ via $f$. Apply [thm-fin-proper-constructibility-complete] to $f$, now a proper morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes. It gives $\mathcal C(f)$. By [def-finrepair-property-c], with precisely the finite allowable coefficient ring of the statement and the given constructible $F$, this means $R^qf_*F$ is constructible for every $q\geq0$. This predicate includes no vanishing assertion, so the dimension bound will be proved separately.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: constructibility from thm-fin-proper-constructibility-complete

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$. Choose an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ containing its image. The finite affine cover from step 1 pulls back to a finite cover of $X_{\bar s}$ by $\operatorname{Spec}(B_{ij}\otimes_{A_i}\Omega)$: affine fibre products are tensor products [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. If $B_{ij}=A_i[b_1,\ldots,b_r]$, then $B_{ij}\otimes_{A_i}\Omega$ is generated over $\Omega$ by $b_1\otimes1,\ldots,b_r\otimes1$. Hence $X_{\bar s}$ is of finite type over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The assumed bound gives $\dim X_{\bar s}\leq d$. The image of $N$ is a unit in $\Omega$, since $N$ is a unit in $A_i$ and its inverse maps to an inverse under $A_i\to\Omega$.

Put $F_{\bar s}=i_{\bar s}^{-1}F$, where $i_{\bar s}:X_{\bar s}\to X$ is the first projection. By [prop-constructible-pullback], applied in the category of $\Lambda$-module sheaves, this pullback is constructible: its finite stratification is the pullback of a stratification for $F$, and its restrictions are finite locally constant. To retain the constructible-subset requirement of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], each pulled-back stratum has constructible underlying subset by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage]. Thus $F_{\bar s}$ satisfies exactly the constructibility hypothesis of the fibre cohomology bound, for the same finite allowable $\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 095G (lemma-pullback-constructible), proof by pulling back the finite partition

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], every geometric stalk of $F$ is finite: the point lies in one of the strata and the restriction there is lisse with finite stalks. Thus $F$ is a finite sheaf in the precise stalkwise sense of [def-constructible-finite]. Apply the sheaf clause of [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] to the proper $f$, the finite ring $\Lambda$, and this finite $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$. For every $q\geq0$ it gives the $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\cong H^q(X_{\bar s},F_{\bar s})$. No global constancy of $F$, and no finiteness of its higher cohomology groups, is asserted.

For $q>2d$, [fin4-lem-fibrewise-cohomological-dimension] applies with $k'=\Omega$, the finite-type scheme $X_{\bar s}$ of dimension at most $d$ from step 3, and the constructible finite allowable coefficient sheaf $F_{\bar s}$ from step 4. It gives $H^q(X_{\bar s},F_{\bar s})=0$. By step 5, $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}=0$. The point was arbitrary, so all geometric stalks vanish.

Let $G=R^qf_*F$ for $q>2d$. The unique morphism $0\to G$ of underlying abelian etale sheaves is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk by step 6. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], it is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. Its inverse is automatically $\Lambda$-linear: every section of $G$ is zero and hence there is only one possible map to the zero module. Thus $G=0$ as a $\Lambda$-module sheaf. Together with step 2 this proves both clauses.
